newsitem.title: BRAZIL: SOCCER-SANTANA TO RETURN AS PALMEIRAS COACH.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-SANTANA TO RETURN AS PALMEIRAS COACH.

text.p: Former Brazil coach Tele Santana, who has been out of soccer for almost a year because of ill health, will be the new coach of Palmeiras, the club said on Thursday.

Santana, who coached Brazil at the 1982 and 1986 World Cups, was forced to abandon his job with Sao Paulo early this year because of health problems. Earlier this week he turned down an offer to coach crisis-hit Fluminense.
He will take up his job with Palmeiras in February, just before the start of the new Brazilian season.

During five years with Sao Paulo Santana won the Brazilian championship once, the South American Libertadores Cup twice and the Intercontinental Cup twice despite having to repeatedly rebuild the team after top players were sold abroad.
Santana, who works on the principle that is better to lose playing attractive soccer than to win playing with a defensive, negative style, is admired worldwide for his spirit of adventure.
He is also a disclipinarian, perfectionist and outspoken critic of Brazilian soccer authorities.
The 1982 World Cup side is regarded by many as one of the best teams in soccer history, even though they did not win the World Cup.
Santana replaces Vanderley Luxemburgo who resigned to take on a job with Pele's former club Santos after just over a year in charge.
Palmeiras were in dynamic form in the first half of the season when they scored 102 goals in 30 games on their way to winning the Sao Paulo championship.
They were less successful in the Brazilian championship, played in the second half of the season. They were knocked out in the quarter-finals by arch-rivals Gremio who went on to win the competition.
